experiment_a.title: Experiment A: Process Death & Memory Loss
experiment_a.empirical_finding: When the process dies via SIGKILL/os._exit, 100% of in-memory EventStore and workflow state disappears. Disk/durable persistence is empirically required for v0.3 restart recovery.

experiment_b.title: Experiment B: Crash Point Injection (Side-Effect Windows)

b2_mid_execution.ambiguity: HIGH (Side effect occurred, but completion event uncommitted in EventStore)

b3_post_execution.ambiguity: LOW (Side effect completed and event committed prior to process termination)

experiment_c.title: Experiment C: Side-Effect Deduplication & Idempotency
experiment_c.empirical_finding: Passing event_id as idempotency_key to external handlers empirically eliminates duplicate side-effect mutations upon workflow replay.

experiment_d.title: Experiment D: Evidence-Based Recovery State Taxonomy

RECOVERABLE.evidence_criteria: EventStore log contains PRE-EXECUTION state (B1) or full POST-EXECUTION event commit (B3) with confirmed idempotency token.

IN_DOUBT.evidence_criteria: Crash injection occurred at MID-EXECUTION (B2) where side effect was initiated but completion event is missing from journal.
IN_DOUBT.action: Suspend automated execution; escalate to operator CLI or require idempotency-key retry.

UNRECOVERABLE.evidence_criteria: EventStore journal log is unreadable, corrupted, or causal hash lineage is broken.
UNRECOVERABLE.action: Permanent halt; flag unrecoverable corruption to operator.

experiment_e.title: Experiment E: Limits of In-Process Compensation
experiment_e.empirical_finding: Automated in-process rollback/compensation on non-reversible side effects is mathematically incomplete without explicit plugin-level idempotency contracts.

five_core_empirical_questions.1_what_survives_process_death: Zero in-memory state survives SIGKILL/os._exit. EventStore requires durable disk serialization for v0.3 restart recovery.
five_core_empirical_questions.2_which_crash_windows_create_ambiguity: Crash Window B2 (MID-EXECUTION) creates maximum ambiguity because external side effect executed but journal event was uncommitted.
five_core_empirical_questions.3_can_duplicate_side_effects_be_reproduc: YES. Without idempotency keys, replaying an event stream after a B2 crash caused 2 mutations for 1 operation.
five_core_empirical_questions.4_does_idempotency_key_eliminate_duplica: YES. Using event_id as an idempotency key reduced duplicate mutations from 2 to 1 on replay.
five_core_empirical_questions.5_evidence_justifying_classifications: Evidence criteria: B1/B3 commits -> RECOVERABLE; B2 uncommitted side effects -> IN_DOUBT; Corrupted journal DAG -> UNRECOVERABLE.

summary.recommendation: Proceed to Phase 3 (Issue #14 Worker Process Boundary) with empirical proof of side-effect ambiguity and idempotency deduplication contracts.
